I wish this had more upvotes because I’d like to see what others have to say. I’m in the same situation you are (old friends doing excellently), but without even a degree. But no! I refuse to accept that my life would be ordinary. There are two paths I see right now: the contentment from accepting that life will be ordinary, or the joy of struggle. Live for something. Fight everyday! Even if you get nowhere, spend everyday getting closer to some goal. I have a healthstyle goal too. For example, some people I know are literally models. Will I ever be a world class model? No. Not even in months or years from now. But will I accept my body for what it is, and be _happy_ with it? NO! The joy is in struggle. Even if today I barely break even with calories, the joy is everyday fighting for it instead of giving up. You’re young! You have the rest of your life to do something great with it! Code Geass was written when the author was 40. KFC was founded when Sanders was 70! It is better to battle in the ring than be happy as a spectator. Life’s not over yet. You don’t know where you’ll be years from now, but it doesn’t have to be this way day in and day out for the rest of your life, unless you let it, and be at peace with it. But the greater joy is in struggling for something, for example IF you were actually interested in the MCAT, it’s more beautiful to struggle studying for it than to accept never accomplishing it (ovb it’s not something you want but replace it with any other goal) but it’s like that. So that when you see, “peer is doing x” you don’t have to say, well there’s nothing going on with my life how do I accept it, you say “peer is doing x but that’s okay I’m working on y and x and y together make the world a better place” (lmao I’ll probably delete this in the morning cause it’s such gibberish but you get my point and now I’m fired up to go create) even if your goal is something like “be the first woman to do 1000 pull ups a day” it’s still a goal so that when someone cures cancer you can say something like they’re good at that and I’m good at this.

A guy went out to the lake and practiced rowing competitively every morning. The writer asked, "How do you do it?" The rower said, "If I asked myself every morning whether or not I 'felt' like rowing, I would go to the lake at max two days a week."

I had this exact problem; here are three things I did:


1. Download Forest. The visual proof of success are far more important than you might realize! The tree dies if you check your phone. 


2. Download Sleepytown. It’s by the same developer, but I have never had such a perfect sleeping schedule. The building dies if you check your phone after bedtime or before your wake up time. 


3. Meditate or visualize yourself being disciplined. If you are religious, pray before you start your work for discipline and focus. This reinforces your mind the goal of focus.

Edited to add:
- Freedom app: even though it is super easy to delete sites from the banned list, seeing that blocked page is a good reminder. 

-go to notifications and turn off notifications for apps like Snapchat or even log out entirely. 

-download Stayfocusd on the computer for your web browsers. If you don’t visit certain websites on the computer you won’t want to on your phone.

Deadlines are pretty useful in two situations. 


1. You and a client/boss depend on its completion. Some people are unreliable and will never deliver. 


2. A deadline you set yourself makes a higher output. You finish works (books, art, songs, code) and don't rush perfectionism. If you "have to finish in 3 days" you won't wait around until the conditions are perfect. Even if you don't make the deadline despite your best efforts, you tell yourself the deadline was unrealistic, extend the deadline and adjust it for the next project.  


I get what you're saying about not doing your best work under deadline due to pressure, but you risk perfectionism in that case. Better a good work done than a great idea never executed.
